title: Changing the customer on an open work order takes the new customer's term
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds Net 30 and customer {Customer-B} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due on day 10 of the following month.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-08 First, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-08 Second and {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-08 Tenth.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15444.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On {Work-order-1}, change the customer to {Customer-B}.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the work order now shows {Customer-B}.
  • Step 2: the invoice preview shows.
  • Step 3: the due date reads Nov 10, 2026 ({Term-A}, not Net 30's Nov 4).
  • Step 4: the invoice shows {Term-A} and due Nov 10, 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-E4: “If the customer on an open work order or part sale is changed, the invoice takes the new customer's term at invoicing, by the same rule. Nothing about the term is copied onto the work order or part sale before invoicing.”
